situation:
You are the practice administrator at LAKESHORE FAMILY DENTAL GROUP, eleven clinics opening their first location in a neighboring state. The regional director (judge) has asked you to recommend how the flagship clinic's daily schedule should be covered for the next six months, and who should carry what.

Two of the flagship's four hygienists have been assigned to open the new clinic. A third has asked to work reduced hours for a personal medical reason and has asked that the reason stay between the two of you. That leaves the clinic short of the hours its standing recall patients have booked, some of them for more than a decade.

One course adds an evening rotation shared by the whole team, which keeps every patient's standing slot. The clinic's last staff survey already named workload as its lowest-rated item, and a rotation nobody is exempt from would either force the third hygienist onto evenings or make that exemption plain to everyone. The other course moves patients on the shortest recall to a longer interval.

That protects the team's hours but tells long-standing patients they will be seen less often, and the hygienists who built those relationships would make the calls. The regional director (judge) wants your recommendation and how you would explain it to the people it lands hardest on. The director (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, then thank you after your presentation and questions.
